column6: The device's own answer (rule 1): alpha-to-coverage at one sample. Metal's covers the pixel only above an alpha of 1/2, so the draw's 0.5 covers nothing and the destination stays (Metal 255); lavapipe's covers it, by a 2x2 ordered dither, and stores the fragment (ours 64, its 0.25 as a code). column6: The device's own answer (rule 1), a known gap of the runtime (its README, Known gaps of textures): a runtime sampler of an opaque-black border, clamp to border on `s` and `t`, sampled past the texture's edge; the RTX 3090 reads the border's alpha as 1, where Metal reads `A8Unorm`'s one channel from the border colour's red, 0 (the `bgra` swizzle moves no channel); the 780M and llvmpipe read Metal's 0. The runtime holds `A8Unorm` in `R8_UNORM` read through a view that moves red to alpha, `(0, 0, 0, r)`, on every device (it uses Vulkan 1.3 and does not enable `VK_KHR_maintenance5`, so `A8_UNORM` is not exposed), and the device reads the border through that mapping only with `borderColorSwizzleFromImage`, which the 3090's driver does not report. A sampler in the arrays meets every view, so no create info names the view's mapping. The first differing element is at [image 0, row 1, 11] (U32, byte 124): Metal 0 (0x0), ours 1065353216 (0x3f800000). Note `swizzled-opaque-black-border`.

Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the source product to the attachment's precision and carrying the destination product into the sum unrounded (`round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)`, measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, from this family's committed recordings), and `metal2vulkan-runtime` leaves the blend to the device's fixed-function unit, whose results are its own. Under the native-arithmetic contract the device's blend is the answer: `device-color-conversion`, which the run announces, records a float attachment's blend as the device's arithmetic, and validation derives no tolerance from it; its recorded bounds do not cover a float attachment's blend, so what is open is that bound. Open: nothing in the product; folding the blend into the function to reproduce Metal's bits is the emulation the native-arithmetic contract rules out.

Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the source product to the attachment's precision and carrying the destination product into the sum unrounded (`round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)`, measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, from this family's committed recordings), and `metal2vulkan-runtime` leaves the blend to the device's fixed-function unit, whose results are its own. Under the native-arithmetic contract the device's blend is the answer: `device-color-conversion`, which the run announces, records a float attachment's blend as the device's arithmetic, and validation derives no tolerance from it; its recorded bounds do not cover a float attachment's blend, so what is open is that bound. Open: nothing in the product; folding the blend into the function to reproduce Metal's bits is the emulation the native-arithmetic contract rules out.

column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("texture slot 0, which a function samples through a bicubic filter, bound to a RGBA8UnormSRGB texture, whose bicubic sample is not built"))
column6: Known gap (the rt README, Known gaps of textures): a function's bicubic constexpr sample of a texture of 8-bit sRGB codes is `Gap::BicubicTexels`, naming the slot and the format. Metal sums the decoded taps; the runtime holds the texture as an sRGB image and builds no bicubic sample of it. The fix belongs in the bicubic routine's sRGB arm (`lower::sampler::bicubic`), built when a stream binds one.

column6: The device's arithmetic under the static note `bicubic-filter-arithmetic` (rule 1), within its stated bound. Metal's results lie on the format's grid: a sixteenth of a code for the 8-bit classes, a whole code for `RGBA16Unorm`, an exact `half` for `RGBA16Float`; at the six `RGBA16Float` samples where the sum is exactly halfway between two halves, Metal rounds away from zero. Ours is the unrounded `f32` sum of the sixteen decoded taps (the 2D routine, `lower::sampler::bicubic::routines`, `Plane`), and a `half` result is the device's narrowing of it. Every class takes Metal's arm, which the case's own tests hold in Metal's recording: `R32Float` the inner bilinear taps, which compare exactly; the clamp into [0, 1] of the unsigned normalized formats and into [-1, 1] of `RGBA8Snorm`; no clamp of `RGBA16Float`.
